traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for Story `docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md` are fully implemented and covered by tests:
1. **File-Level Template (@supports with placeholders)** - Implemented by `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` and `buildSupportsTemplateComment`, which insert a JSDoc `@supports` block at the top of test files that lack one, using the placeholder path `docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ` plus a clear TODO line. - Tested in `tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts` via the invalid case for `[REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE]`, with explicit `output` verifying the inserted template.
2. **Format Fixes for malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes** - Implemented in `normalizeReqId` and `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription`, invoked from `handleItOrTestCall` with ESLint fixers. They normalize: - `[ REQ-XXX ]` → `[REQ-XXX]` - `[REQ_XXX]` → `[REQ-XXX]` - `(REQ-XXX)` → `[REQ-XXX]` - `[req-xxx]` → `[REQ-XXX]` - Verified by multiple invalid tests in `require-test-traceability.test.ts` for `[REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT]`, each with an `output` string asserting the corrected prefix.
3. **Template Quality and Placeholders** - Template includes both a structured placeholder line and a human-readable TODO: `TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file.` - Tests assert the exact multi-line template (including the TODO text), ensuring clarity and consistency (REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER).
4. **Quality Standards & Preservation of Behavior/Formatting** - Auto-fixes only touch comments (`@supports` block) and test name string literals; no implementation code is changed. - String literals are rewritten via `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw`, which preserves the original quoting style and escapes, so runtime behavior and most formatting remain intact (REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE). - Safety checks ensure fixers are only attached when the first argument is a string literal and a normalized prefix exists.
5. **Integration with ESLint --fix & existing rules** - Rule `traceability/require-test-traceability` declares `meta.fixable: "code"` and uses standard ESLint fixer callbacks, so `eslint --fix` will apply these changes. - The rule is documented and enabled alongside other core rules in presets, and its tests use ESLint’s `RuleTester` with `output` expectations, confirming integration with the ESLint workflow.
6. **User Experience (consistent, easy templates)** - A single, consistent default template is used across files; users can override it via the `testSupportsTemplate` option if desired. - The inserted block is clearly marked as a placeholder with TODO guidance, making it straightforward to complete.
7. **Error Handling and Safety (only guaranteed-safe fixes)** - If no `@supports` exists, the rule either reports without a fixer (when `autoFixTestTemplate === false`) or adds the placeholder comment; it never attempts to infer a real story path or REQ IDs. - For REQ prefixes, normalization only occurs when the description already starts with a recognizable REQ token; descriptions without any REQ prefix produce an error but **no** auto-fix (explicitly tested as `[REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE]`). - Fixers are guarded by type checks and normalization results, so no speculative transformations are applied.
8. **Documentation** - `user-docs/api-reference.md` includes a detailed description of the `traceability/require-test-traceability` rule’s auto-fix behavior, explicitly calling out the placeholder template, TODO guidance, and prefix normalization constraints. - This satisfies the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the concrete implementation in `src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts` and its helpers, the comprehensive tests in `tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts`, passing CI tests, and the user-facing documentation, Story 021.0 is fully implemented and verified.
